newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada to phase in tobacco sponsorship rules.
newsitem.headline: Canada to phase in tobacco sponsorship rules.

text.p: Health Minister David Dingwall agreed on Wednesday to give tobacco companies one year to adjust to new restrictions on their sponsorship of sporting and cultural events.
Dingwall said he had introduced an amendment to an overall anti-tobacco bill now before the House of Commons in the Canadian Parliament.

The House Health Committee had recommended in December, after an outcry from areas like Montreal and Toronto which benefit from the events, that the sponsorship restrictions be phased in. It did not suggest a time frame, however.
"It's very reasonable and we think it doesn't detract from the principals of our bill at all," Dingwall told the Canadian Broadcasting Corporation.
"It's not a cultural bill. It's not a sports bill. It's a health bill."
Anti-smoking groups like the Canadian Medical Association had voiced concern that the minister would weaken the bill in response to intensive lobbying by the tobacco industry and its supporters.

The opposition Bloc Quebecois said on Wednesday the one-year grace period was simply a means of avoiding further controversy over tobacco sponsorship until after the federal elections expected later this year.

"Rather than really looking for a solution to the question of sponsorship by tobacco companies, Health Minister David Dingwall is simply postponing the implementation of measures contested with yesterday's proposed changes to his anti-smoking bill," said the Bloc's Antoine Dube.
Imperial Tobacco Ltd, a unit of Imasco Ltd controls about 65 percent of the Canadian cigarette market. Imasco is 40 percent owned by B.A.T. Industries Plc of Britain.
The second biggest player, Rothmans, Benson and Hedges Inc, owned 60 percent by Rothmans Inc, a unit of Rothmans International Plc, and 40 percent by Philip Morris Cos Inc.
Third place holder RJR MacDonald is wholly owned by RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp unit R.J. Reynolds Tobacco International.
